savings_reason: EO 9901 conferred the same functions, duties and authority under Executive Orders 7057, 7180 (as amended by 7554) and 7689 on James P. earlier_end_check: The packet's Cruden number-citation lookup over the 33,118 held order-text files finds no other held text citing EO 9618 by number. The later-events catalog search recorded 4 machine hits and the name search 1 hit (EO 9901); no held text shows an earlier revocation, resignation date or supersession. The earliest held instrument showing that Arnold had resigned and been replaced is EO 9901. The order states no term, until-date or condition.
scope_check: One operative clause, matching the machine inventory (EO:9618#whole): the paragraph that appoints Arnold, directs that he serve without additional compensation and exercise the functions conferred by Executive Orders 7057, 7180 (as amended by 7554) and 7689, and amends those orders accordingly. savings_check: The functions were conferred on the individual appointee; EO 9901 re-conferred them on the successor in the same terms, so the residual is a transfer, not a surviving command of EO 9618. Parker became unable to serve, and provides that the sixty-day period in paragraph 1 of EO 9611 begins to run on the date of this order. Page location was checked against the PDF page markers of the held text layer only; no page image was inspected. The representation is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, held as original_representation_unverified. The period of the Board's re-establishment is fixed by EO 9611 paragraph 1 and restarted by this order; the end below follows from this order's own sentence about the period.
savings_reason: The order contains no savings or transfer clause. Its two commands (the new membership of the Board and the start of the sixty-day period) have no residual effect once the Board's period ended, and the machine searches of the U.S. Code and the eCFR and the Federal Register catalog return no hit citing EO 9627. Whether the direction in paragraph 3 of EO 9611 that the War Shipping Administration be guided by the Board's determination survived the Board's period concerns EO 9611, not this order, and is not decided here.
earlier_end_check: The dossier chain for EO 9627 is empty, the later-events catalog search has no hit, and the packet's Cruden number-citation lookup over the 33,118 held order-text files finds no other held text citing EO 9627 by number. The order's own sentence, "The period of sixty days specified in" paragraph 1 "of the said Order" shall begin to run on the date of this order, gives the end. EO 9611 allows an earlier end 'for such shorter period of time as may be required for the completion of its functions'; no held source shows that the Board completed its functions or was discharged earlier, so no earlier dated end is claimed. Neither a report deadline nor a later amendment ends the clause.
scope_check: One operative clause, matching the machine inventory (EO:9627#whole): the amendment of paragraph 2 of EO 9611 (new membership) together with the sentence starting the sixty-day period. The recital that Judge Parker is unable to serve is not a command. The order amends only paragraph 2 and the start of the period; it leaves paragraphs 1 and 3 of EO 9611 otherwise as they were.
independent_command_check: Both commands in the clause (membership of the Board as amended, and the start date of the sixty days) are tied to the existence of the Board and end with its period; neither is an appointment of a person to an office that outlasts the Board, a delegation or a report direction.
savings_check: Nothing in the order or in a held source shows a residual duty or right of this order after the Board's period; the surviving question about paragraph 3 of EO 9611 is outside this order's text.
